A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same LPAM study, and all supplied pages, equations, tables and figures are readable. Neither contains appendices or embedded attachments. However, v3 refers to supplementary visual comparisons, patch-size discussion and timing analyses that are not included, limiting comparison of those materials.

before.justification: v2 reports original seam-quality, global-alignment and runtime measurements on three image datasets in Tables I–III, alongside qualitative experiments.

after.justification: v3 reports original experimental results in Tables 1–4, including retained seam-quality measurements and new alignment-method comparisons and quantitative ablations.

M1.justification: The core LPAM pipeline remains. However, Eq. (4) changes the stated displacement from f(V(p)) to the spatially weighted vector f(p)·V(p), and final composition is described as direct seam-based compositing instead of gradient-domain fusion. These are revisions to the written procedure; they do not establish that the implementation changed.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate large-parallax image stitching using 35 Parallax pairs, 24 SEAGULL pairs and the same 20-pair custom dataset. The added alignment methods and parameter sweeps vary configurations within this retained coverage.

E2.justification: v3 Table 2 substantially expands the paired comparisons beyond REW: Baseline without and with LPAM is evaluated after Homo, ANAP, GSP and UDIS++ alignment. The existing Baseline, Perception, Iterative and Quaternion seam-cutting comparisons, and the Microsoft ICE, Parallax and SEAGULL visual comparators, remain.

E3.justification: v3 adds evaluation across five alignment methods and quantitative experiments varying sigmoid strength and seam-assessment patch size, while fixing scoring patches at 21×21. It removes the global-overlap accuracy evaluation and changes the reported final compositing procedure. Dataset sizes, principal seam metrics, default parameters and hardware remain unchanged; rerunning existing experiments is not established.

E4.justification: v3 extends v2 Figure 3's qualitative sigmoid comparison into a quantitative ablation covering sigmoid removal, five beta values and six patch sizes across all datasets. It also adds robustness evidence across alignment methods. Conversely, v2's global-alignment analysis and demonstrated failure of the seam-plausibility test are absent from the supplied v3 PDF; the small-patch failure remains.

E5.justification: Neither supplied PDF reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests. Both present point estimates.

E6.justification: v3 adds the alignment-method and ablation results in Tables 2–3 and omits v2 Table II's global-alignment results. Nine values change in the shared Baseline+LPAM row: for example, Parallax PSNR changes from 31.90 to 31.85 and SEAGULL PSNR from 28.31 to 28.84. Other shared seam-quality rows and all runtime values remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Eq. (4) receives a substantive algebraic correction: the sigmoid weights the displacement vector using pixel position, replacing the earlier expression applying it directly to the vector. The energy objective, seam-quality criterion, sigmoid definition and evaluation formulas otherwise remain, with no new theorems or proofs.

C1.justification: The central contribution remains an efficient, modular LPAM for existing seam-cutting methods. v3 additionally makes explicit priority and scope claims: the first modular framework and an alignment-compensation paradigm that dissociates seam quality from initial alignment accuracy. These strengthen the positioning of the retained contribution.

C2.justification: v3 removes the warning that the unchanged plausibility test can accept a broadly misaligned seam and extract no patches. It replaces the local no-or-small-parallax assumption with an explanation involving insufficient feature correspondences in texture-deficient regions. New ablation interpretation discusses better seam metrics despite artifacts outside patches and patch-size tradeoffs; the small-patch smoothness limitation remains.

D1.justification: Algorithm 1 now explicitly documents intermediate image updates and realigned-image outputs. v3 omits v2's explicit MATLAB implementation and dataset-in-repository statements, while retaining the same code link, hardware and default settings. This changes documentation, without establishing a change in implementation language or resource availability.

R1.justification: v3 adds references for GSP, ANAP, UDIS++ and RBF-based alignment, and removes v2 references [5], [12] and [35], including Poisson image editing. Most related-work discussion remains intact, although novelty positioning now explicitly asserts the first modular framework.

P1.justification: v3 substantially rewrites the abstract, introduction, contribution statements and conclusion. It separates patch alignment and seam merging into subsections and reorganizes quantitative evaluation around seam-cutting methods, alignment methods and ablations. This is extensive narrative revision beyond simply inserting new results.

P2.justification: v3 adds two full-width tables, removes the global-alignment table, revises the overview diagram and reduces the dataset montage to one column. It removes and rearranges panels of the failure figure, relocates existing displays and changes the document's typography and layout. Most underlying photographic examples are retained.

improvement.justification: The corrected warp formula and Tables 2–3 improve technical clarity and validation of alignment compatibility and parameter sensitivity. However, v3 removes a demonstrated failure of its unchanged seam-selection rule while strengthening alignment-independence claims. Additional supporting analyses are referenced only in unavailable supplementary material. These substantive gains and losses prevent a reliable judgment of the net quality direction from the supplied PDFs.
